channel.title: North Wales Chronicle - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from North Wales Chronicle (northwaleschronicle.co.uk)

item.title: £202 million DWP Cold Weather Payments paid out, how to see if you qualify
item.description: More than £202 million was paid out in Cold Weather Payments over the last three winters, including more than £137 million in the 2022 to 2023 winter alone.

item.title: North Wales holiday park company wins three British Travel Awards prizes
item.description: A holiday park company in North Wales has won gold and bronze prizes at this year’s British Travel Awards.

item.title: Passengers denied entry to Holyhead-to-Cardiff train which was ‘too busy’
item.description: Passengers trying to board a train at Prestatyn railway station last weekend were refused entry because of how busy it was.

item.title: LIVE: Weather updates from across North Wales as Storm Bram hits
item.description: Storm Bram has brought heavy wind and rain to North Wales today, after the Met Office issued a yellow weather warning affecting most of the region.

item.title: Gwynedd main road closes due to flooding as Storm Bram hits region
item.description: A main road in Gwynedd has closed due to flooding, as the region feels the full force of Storm Bram.

item.title: Storm Bram: All the latest flood alerts in place across Gwynedd and Anglesey
item.description: Storm Bram continues to wreak havoc across North Wales today (December 9) with several flood alerts issued by Natural Resources Wales (NRW).

item.title: Train services between Holyhead and Bangor 'disrupted' by heavy rain
item.description: Train services between Holyhead and Bangor have been disrupted due to heavy rain brought on by Storm Bram.

item.title: Anglesey: Man left former partner ‘seeing stars’ and in ‘searing pain’
item.description: A man left his former partner “seeing stars” and in “searing pain” after assaulting and strangling her in her Anglesey home.

item.title: Crackdown on North Wales trains to ensure safe journeys during Christmas
item.description: Transport for Wales and British Transport Police are increasing patrols across the rail network this December as operations return to improve safety.

item.title: Betsi under fire for removing sandwiches from North Wales emergency department
item.description: Ysbyty Glan Clwyd has now stopped providing sandwiches in the emergency department, despite some patients being left for hours in corridors before they are seen.
